name: interactive-hover-button
title: Interactive Hover Button
description: A rounded button whose small dot grows to flood the whole pill when hovered. The resting label drifts away and a second copy with a right arrow slides in.
use: A primary call to action wants a moment of motion without changing its size or the layout.
avoid: Touch-first layouts, where hover never fires, and labels people need to keep reading while they aim.
a11y: The arrow label only appears on hover, so keyboard and touch users never see the finished state. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Inside a dark card sit a tiny outlined badge, a bold heading and a line of grey copy, with a pill button at the bottom. The button has a thin border, a small round dot at its left and white text; hovered, the pill turns pale and the text dark.
behaves: On hover the dot scales up to cover the button over a third of a second while the first label slides right and fades and a second label with a right arrow slides in. Leaving the button runs the same transition back.
customise: The label is children and is rendered twice, once at rest and once with the arrow on hover; colours follow theme tokens, while size and radius come from className.
weight: light: Two short CSS transitions on a scale and a translate, idle when not hovered.
demo: Badge "New in v2.4", heading "Ship interfaces faster", explanatory copy and a button labelled Get started
issues: The hovered label sits grey on a pale pill, noticeably weaker contrast than at rest.
polishWhy: Crisp motion and clear hierarchy; the hovered label's contrast is the weak point.
